correctness.rationale: The arithmetic-state transition updates the exact quotient of the shifted input and the capped boundary run, with parity of fully contained \(1^m\) blocks. A closed residual formula counts crossing blocks. Distinct parity and trailing-run coordinates have explicit separating continuations; distinct quotient states are separated by continuations \(2^K-q\prime\), where the lower quotient residual alternates and the higher one does not. For shift \(c=2^r\), positive quotient levels are disjoint and contain exactly \(A_m(k)\) parity-run pairs, with one exceptional state at \(r=m\); the zero-quotient region has exactly \(2m\) reachable distinct states. Symbolic counting proves the sum and stable formula. The included partition-refinement program and direct output comparisons corroborate 190 dyadic and 405 additional shifts; finite checks do not prove universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: Exact minimal state complexity is a natural invariant for the recently introduced all-one-run parity family. The result detects a one-state carry threshold correction and then an exact linear regime of slope \(2m\); the structural all-shifts no-merging theorem identifies the complete residual-state geometry, rather than merely supplying a finite bound. It covers every \(m\ge3\) and every dyadic shift, with explicit assumptions and limitations.
